title: Cohort shadow sampler and auto-rollback signal integrator for Console
creator: Aditi Kapoor
description: Build a Console-facing feature that lets product engineers configure a lightweight cohort-based shadow sampler and wire its signals into the auto-rollback advisor. The goal is to provide safe, low-cost shadow traffic sampling, surface divergence signals (latency, token cost, semantic drift, hallucination rate), and feed composite rollback heuristics for canary/A-B rollouts. This ticket scopes the UX flows, success metrics, and integration contract with serving telemetry + the rollout decision engine.
acceptance_criteria: Console UI allows creating a shadow cohort with sampling rate between 0.1% and 10% and selecting routing keys (route, customer id hashing, or session id)
Collected shadow metrics: request latency p50/p95, token cost, response-length, rerank divergence, and hallucination flag per-cohort visible in per-route cohort diff view
Auto-rollback advisor receives normalized divergence score and exposes a recommended action (hold/rollback/continue) with justification in the rollout timeline
Rollout timeline links cohort diff to traces and to the underlying PR/commit (trace-linker implemented) in >= 90% of sampled sessions

End-to-end test: create a canary with 10% traffic and 2% shadow sampling; trigger synthetic drift; Console surfaces recommendation and allow one-click rollback which executes a staged revert (mocked in staging)
decisions: Use client-side hashing on customer_id/session_id for deterministic cohort assignment to avoid sticky server state
Shadow-sampled requests should be routed to the same model variant as the canary but be marked with minimal persistence (no long-term storage of full responses by default)
Composite divergence score will be a weighted sum: 40% semantic drift (embedding distance), 30% latency delta, 20% hallucination rate, 10% token cost; weights are adjustable in future iterations
Default auto-rollback threshold set conservatively to minimize false positives; PM will run a two-week calibration study in staging before lowering thresholds
engineering_notes: ENG owners: please expose a light-weight trace token for each sampled request so Console can link to traces without coupling to full distributed-tracing headers (see ENG-81234)
Telemetry needs an aggregation pipeline that preserves per-route and per-model tags; design for 1M samples/day with 7-day hot retention
We will implement sampling at the edge proxy to avoid adding load to runtime; fallback will be server-side if proxy version not available
Privacy: strip PII from saved response snapshots; only store model outputs and normalized metrics by default

qa_plan: Create synthetic canary and shadow cohorts in staging; run 48h to capture baseline metrics
Inject divergence by altering model candidate to return high hallucination prompts and verify Console flags hallucination spike
End-to-end rollback smoke test: user executes Console rollback; verify route config flips within SLA and traffic drains according to policy
Trace-linking audit: sample 100 traced requests from shadow cohort and validate clickable trace opens distributed trace view
risks: High telemetry volume could increase ingestion cost; mitigation: adjustable sampling cap and embedding compute fraction
False positive rollbacks due to noisy metrics; mitigation: conservative thresholds and require multi-metric agreement before recommend rollback
Privacy/regulatory exposure if full responses are stored; mitigation: default to storing hashed identifiers and aggregated metrics, encrypted snapshot storage when enabled
